deep_analysis.executive_intro:
This FTSE screen is broadly neutral-to-cautious: 143 holds dominate versus 17 strong buys and 43 avoids, so actionable value is concentrated rather than market-wide. Among the five top-ranked names, three sit in Industrials (FGP.L, MEGP.L, GFTU.L), with ITV.L in Communication Services and HIK.L as the lone Healthcare name — a tilt toward cyclical/industrial exposure rather than financials or tech. All five carry “new” signals (one week at rating) with conviction scores in the 46–53% range, so quantitative support is fresh but not yet time-tested. A key caution: several top picks were downgraded from strong buy to buy after FCF-basis overlays, and filing-aligned versus company-adjusted free cash flow diverge materially on ITV.L, FGP.L, and HIK.L — yield- and value-dependent model passes may overstate economic cash generation until those figures are reconciled manually.

**ITV.L (ITV plc)** — The highest composite score in the set (91%, 15/22 models, sector-relative 88%), passing all five factor families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk). Standout passes include Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.51, earnings growth 23%), High Dividend Yield (7.0%), and Composite Value; key metrics are P/E 11.8, P/B 1.5, ROE 13.5%. Failures are notable on quality/momentum: Piotroski F-Score 3/9, Buffett Quality, and Economic Moat (ROE below 18%, thin margins). An FCF basis overlay flagged filing £148M vs screen TTM £211.9M vs company-adjusted £325M, and the signal was adjusted to Buy. No sector concentration issue beyond being the sole media name. **Verdict: watchlist** — headline cheapness and yield are compelling, but FCF divergence and a weak Piotroski score warrant reconciliation before sizing a position.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Strong cheapness and GARP profile: 13/22 models (composite 86%, sector-relative 87%), passing Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield (E/P 11.2%), FCF Yield (7.9%), Lynch PEG (PEG 0.56, growth 16%), Piotroski F-Score 8/9, and Composite Value; P/E 8.9, P/B 1.4, ROE 16.7%, yield 4.0%. Offsetting this, Financial Health fails (debt/equity 161%, current ratio 0.73), as do Quality Value and Buffett Quality on leverage and thin margins. FCF basis mismatch is severe: filing £362.6M, screen TTM £302.8M, company-adjusted £73.8M — signal adjusted to Buy. Adds to the Industrials cluster alongside MEGP.L and GFTU.L. **Verdict: watchlist** — valuation and improving fundamentals look attractive, but leverage, weak liquidity, and unresolved FCF definitions are blockers to accumulation.

**HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC)** — Ten of 22 models pass (composite 81%, sector-relative 91%), leaning quality-over-yield: Graham Enterprising, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, and Financial Health; P/E 12.5, P/B 1.9, ROE 15.4%, yield 3.9%. Cheapness screens fail — FCF Yield (3.6%, below 5%), Lynch PEG (growth 1.7%, PEG 7.17), Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion) — and a healthcare price-erosion overlay adjusted the signal to Buy. FCF filing $119M vs screen TTM $14.4M diverges sharply; net FCF dividend coverage is 0.64×. Sole Healthcare name, so no intra-sector clustering. **Verdict: watchlist** — sector-relative cheapness and quality passes are offset by stalled growth, cash-conversion weakness, and pricing-pressure flags.

**MEGP.L (ME Group International plc)** — Fifteen of 22 models pass (composite 81%, sector-relative 87%), one of the broadest pass sets: Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat (ROE 28.2%, margin 17.6%), High Dividend Yield (6.5%), and Magic Formula; P/E 8.7, P/B 2.5. Lynch PEG fails (growth 0.4%, PEG 23.87), and an interim-quality overlay notes declining interim EPS with net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84× (gross 1.68×), adjusting signal to Buy. RSI 68 is elevated. Second Industrials name in the top five. **Verdict: watchlist** — exceptional headline quality and cheapness, but near-stagnant earnings growth and sub-1× net dividend coverage argue against accumulation until interim trends clarify.

**GFTU.L (Grafton Group plc)** — Ten of 22 models pass (composite 82%, sector-relative 80%), and it is the only top candidate retaining an unadjusted Strong Buy. Notable passes include Graham Defensive (P/E 12.7, P/B 1.21, current ratio 2.11), FCF Yield (8.2%), Piotroski F-Score 8/9, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health (D/E 38%); yield 3.6%, ROE 8.4%. Failures cluster on deep-value and growth screens (Deep Value, Lynch PEG, Economic Moat, Magic Formula) reflecting modest ROE and 5.1% earnings growth. FCF dividend coverage net is 2.32× with no FCF basis overlay flagged. Third Industrials name — meaningful sector concentration if building a basket from this list. **Verdict: accumulate** — the cleanest balance sheet, cash conversion, and signal integrity in the group, accepting cyclical building-materials exposure and limited moat scores.

- ITV.L: UK broadcast advertising is highly cyclical; structural shift from linear TV to streaming may compress ad revenue independently of current P/E. Pension deficit and content-commitment liabilities are not in the screen — open question.
- ITV.L: Governance and strategic direction (studio/IP vs. traditional broadcasting mix) are not captured; management capital-allocation track record needs manual review.
- FGP.L: UK/US public-transport operator — contract re-bidding, regulatory fare caps, and fuel/labour inflation are material cyclical/policy risks not modeled.
- FGP.L: Debt/equity 161% and current ratio 0.73 suggest balance-sheet stress the value screen partially flags but does not fully contextualise (lease-adjusted debt, covenant headroom unknown).
- FGP.L: Pension obligations for a large employer — open question; not in payload.
- HIK.L: Generic-drug pricing pressure in the US (screen’s healthcare price-erosion overlay hints at this) can erode margins faster than trailing multiples imply.
- HIK.L: Patent cliffs, FDA/competition dynamics, and pipeline dependency are standard pharma risks absent from quantitative inputs.
- HIK.L: Net FCF dividend coverage 0.64× raises dividend-cut risk if pricing pressure persists — qualitative sustainability concern beyond the yield figure.
- MEGP.L: Photo-booth/vending-style business model — durability of locations, contract churn, and technology disruption (smartphone substitution) not captured.
- MEGP.L: USD reporting with UK listing introduces FX translation risk for UK investors; cyclical exposure to travel/leisure footfall.
- MEGP.L: Interim EPS decline and 0.84× net FCF/dividend coverage suggest the 6.5% yield may be at risk — dividend policy/governance not screened.
- GFTU.L: Building-materials merchant — highly correlated to UK/Ireland construction cycles; screen shows no cyclical overlay but macro downturn risk is material.
- GFTU.L: ROE 8.4% and thin margins (5.4%) indicate limited pricing power in a competitive distribution market.
- GFTU.L: Acquisition-driven growth history (implied by sector) — integration risk and goodwill impairment not in screen; open question.

documents.name: ITV plc
documents.executive_summary: ITV plc screens as a **strong buy** on quantitative cheapness (P/E ~11.8, P/B ~1.5, ~7% yield) with broad model pass rates (15/22), but the investment case is now dominated by the proposed **sale of Media & Entertainment (M&E) to Sky** for up to **£1.6bn**, targeting a **~£950m net cash return** to shareholders and a residual **ITV Studios–centric** listed entity. Filings show a business that has pivoted successfully toward studios and digital (two-thirds of revenue), yet **2025 free cash flow fell sharply** to **£187m** (FY RNS) from **£325m** in 2024, and statutory earnings were distorted by the prior-year BritBox gain. The central debate is whether headline valuation and the Sky proceeds compensate for **UK advertising cyclicality**, **regulatory delay/risk** on the deal (CMA, possible Phase 2, completion potentially **H2 2027**), and **uncertain post-transaction earnings power** for a standalone Studios business.
documents.investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen flags ITV as a classic **value + income** candidate: low P/E, sub-3x P/B, high dividend yield, moderate leverage (debt/equity ~52%), and passes across cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk families (composite score ~91%). Business quality is **mixed but improving strategically**: FY2025 RNS shows **group adjusted EBITA down only 1%** to **£534m** despite **TAR down 5%**, with **ITV Studios external revenue +10%** and **digital revenue +10%** to **£614m**; cost savings of **£63m** and ITVX investment recouped ahead of plan support the “More Than TV” transformation narrative.

For a value investor, the **valuation hook** is twofold: (1) earnings and cash flow from a still-integrated broadcaster–studios group trading below market multiples, and (2) **embedded optionality/catalyst** from the Sky transaction—**£950m net cash return** (ex contingent consideration), **£100m buyback** already announced (Jul 2026 interim), and a simplified **global content IP** story (95,000+ hour library, Zoo 55 digital distribution). Dividend discipline (**5.0p** ordinary, ~**£190m** annually) and **£1.3bn+ liquidity** (FY2025) reinforce the income angle.

However, screen failures on **Graham Defensive, net-net, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, and Piotroski F-Score (3/9)** are consistent with filing evidence: **ROE ~13.5%** (below moat thresholds), **thin broadcast margins**, **working-capital-heavy** production economics, and **FCF basis divergence** (screen notes filing **£148m**, company-adjusted **£325m**, TTM **£212m**). The screen’s FCF overlay already adjusts the headline signal toward **buy**, not unqualified strong buy—deep research **partially confirms** cheapness but **does not fully validate** cash-backed quality at face value.

documents.news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **material and deal-heavy**, not thin.

- **Nov 2025:** ITV confirms **preliminary talks** to sell M&E to Sky for **~£1.6bn**; shares surge (**“ITV shares soar as it holds talks to sell television business to Sky”**, The Guardian, 7 Nov 2025; **“ITV in talks to sell television business to Sky”**, BBC, 7 Nov 2025). Nils Pratley highlights **price, politics, and regulation** risks (The Guardian, 7 Nov 2025).
- **Oct 2025:** **Liberty Global halves stake** via secondary placing; shares sink (**“ITV shares sink after John Malone’s Liberty halves its stake”**, Financial Times, 22 Oct 2025).

- **Jul 2026:** **Sky agrees £1.6bn deal** for ITV broadcasting arm (**“Sky agrees £1.6bn ITV deal”**, Financial Times, 6 Jul 2026; Reuters, 6 Jul 2026). ITV frames deal as **transformative**, **~£950m** shareholder return (**“ITV Calls Sky Deal Transformative as It Plans £950 Million Shareholder Return”**, Yahoo Finance, 9 Jul 2026).
- **Jul 2026:** H1 2026 results—**Studios phasing, World Cup ad boost, £100m buyback**, regulatory timeline (**“ITV PLC (ITVPF) (H1 2026) Earnings Call Highlights”**, Yahoo Finance, 31 Jul 2026).
- **Aug 2026:** Post-deal analyst caution—fair value **~£0.81**, targets **~£0.85** (**“ITV Stock Sees Fair Value Cut After Analyst Caution On Sky Deal”**, Yahoo Finance, 6 Aug 2026).

documents.executive_summary: FirstGroup is a UK-focused bus and rail operator emerging from a deliberate portfolio transition: legacy North American and contracted-rail exposure has been reduced, while First Bus (including London franchising) and a diversified First Rail platform (DfT management-fee TOCs, open access, and rail services) drive adjusted earnings. FY2026 adjusted EPS rose to 20.3p (from 19.4p) on adjusted revenue of £1,718.7m, yet adjusted operating profit was marginally lower at £219.4m as open-access mobilisation and the South Western Railway (SWR) handback weighed on margins. The quantitative screen flags compelling value (P/E ~8.9, yield ~4.0%, Piotroski 8/9), but free-cash-flow definitions diverge materially (£362.6m statutory vs £73.8m company-adjusted), and leverage remains elevated under IFRS 16. The central debate is whether contract wins (London Overground), bus consolidation, and capital returns can sustain earnings growth through UK rail reform and accelerated bus decarbonisation capex.
documents.investment_thesis:
The screen’s Strong Buy rating rests on five passing factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—with 20/20 data quality and standout metrics: P/E 8.9, P/B 1.37, earnings yield, FCF yield (on filing-aligned basis), Lynch/Neff PEG variants, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, and Piotroski F-Score 8/9. That profile fits a value investor seeking a cash-generative industrial at a discount to its own recent earnings trajectory: adjusted EPS has compounded from 16.7p (FY2024) to 19.4p (FY2025) to 20.3p (FY2026), with dividends rising from 5.5p to 6.5p to 7.2p.

Business quality is better than the screen’s leverage-sensitive failures (Graham Defensive, Buffett Quality, Financial Health) imply. Management’s UK-only strategy is delivering visible wins: First Bus London expansion, open-access passenger growth, Rail Services externalisation, and the preferred-operator status for the London Overground contract (RNS, 10 December 2025). Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly—£89m returned in FY2026 via dividends and buybacks, a £100m buyback launched June 2026, and progressive dividend policy tightening toward ~2.5x adjusted-EPS cover. The valuation hook is a mid-single-digit earnings multiple on a business reinvesting in electrification while de-risking the pension bus section (£20m cash returned on triennial valuation completion, H1 2026 report).

For a value investor, the mismatch between statutory and adjusted metrics is the opportunity *and* the diligence item: the screen passes on filing-aligned FCF (£362.6m) and earnings quality, but company-adjusted FCF of £73.8m (FY2026 annual accounts) reflects heavy growth capex and acquisition spend that may be transitional rather than structural.

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary: Hikma is a FTSE 100 multinational generics and injectables group with three engines — US-focused Injectables and Hikma Rx, plus MENA Branded — trading on roughly 12.5× earnings, 1.9× book and a 3.9% dividend yield, which the quantitative screen flags as a **strong buy** (10/22 models; 81% composite). The value case rests on investment-grade balance sheet strength (BBB), durable cash generation, shareholder returns ($250m buyback, rising dividend), and a H1 2026 profit beat that has prompted multiple broker upgrades. The central debate is whether Injectables margin erosion, elevated capex and working-capital build, and the February 2026 withdrawal of medium-term guidance mark a cyclical trough or a structural reset — compounded by an unresolved free-cash-flow measurement gap (filing-aligned FY2025 FCF $119m vs screen TTM $14.4m).
documents.investment_thesis:
The screen’s strong-buy signal is underpinned by breadth across value families: cheapness (P/E 12.5, P/B 1.89, D/E 77%), quality (ROE 15.4%, passes Buffett Quality and Financial Health), dividend (3.9% yield, Dividend Growth model pass), GARP (Neff PEGY, Magic Formula), and risk (Acquirer’s Multiple, Composite Value). Sector-relative composite (91%) is elevated for Healthcare. Business quality is genuine: FY2025 core revenue grew 6% to **$3,349m**, core operating profit rose 3% to **$741m** (22.1% margin), and the group retained S&P/Fitch **BBB** ratings with net debt/core EBITDA at **1.6×** (FY2025 results, 26 February 2026). H1 2026 confirmed operational momentum — core operating profit **+9%** to **$405m** on revenue **+4%** to **$1,728m** — with Branded (+15%) offsetting flat Injectables.

For a value investor, the hook is a quality compounder priced like a distressed generic: statutory earnings recovered (FY2025 profit to shareholders **$402m**, +12%; basic EPS **182 cents**) after a one-off sodium oxybate legal settlement, while the market still prices low single-digit growth (screen: ~1.7% earnings growth; Lynch PEG fails). Capital return is tangible: total FY2025 dividend **84 cents** (+5%), interim H1 2026 **38 cents** (+6%), and **$227m** of the **$250m** buyback completed by 5 August 2026. US manufacturing footprint (Ohio, New Jersey) offers a relative tariff hedge versus import-dependent peers — a point echoed in sell-side commentary. Overlays that temper the raw screen signal to **Buy** (from Strong Buy) — healthcare price-erosion and FCF basis divergence — are worth monitoring but do not invalidate the core cheapness/quality pairing.

post_run_review.executive_summary:
This run is broadly neutral-to-cautious (143 holds vs 17 strong buys and 43 avoids), with buy-tier conviction concentrated in 61 names but top-ranked signals still fresh (46–53% conviction, one week at rating). The largest systemic weakness is **FCF-basis inconsistency**: filing-aligned, screen TTM, and company-adjusted figures diverge materially on ITV.L, FGP.L, and HIK.L, and several names were downgraded from strong buy to buy after FCF overlays—yield- and value-dependent model passes may overstate economic cash generation. A second weakness is **ingest depth vs index breadth**: buy-tier filing indexes are fully bodied (`thin_filing_tickers` empty; `indexed_without_body: 0` across filing_coverage), but initial-mode memo snapshots show low `filings_with_body` ratios (e.g. MEGP.L 16/61, GFTU.L 13/75, GSK.L 20/99), limiting first-pass memo quality to “adequate” (source_quality_score ~0.59–0.69). Gap-fill improved ITV.L, FGP.L, and HIK.L to “strong” memos (0.86–0.96), yet all follow-up questions remain **partially_resolved**—FCF reconciliation, covenant headroom, and US pricing erosion are documented but not closed. These gaps **block full conviction** on top picks: deep analysis assigns watchlist verdicts to all five leaders pending manual FCF and balance-sheet reconciliation.

**Ingest — filing body fetch and classification (dominant backlog theme; 129/287 backlog items, 29/73 recent)**
- Re-pull full RNS/Investegate HTML or PDF bodies instead of Google News wrappers or AI-summary wrappers; recurring for AEP.L (31 indexed, 0 bodies in sample), MEGP.L (52 indexed, 0 bodies), ITV.L, HIK.L, FGP.L.
- Companies House filed-accounts PDF fetch/OCR when bodies missing (AEP.L, ITV.L — five CH refetches returned zero bodies in sample).

**Scoring — FCF basis, overlays, and metadata alignment (69 backlog, 16 recent)**

- Sector misclassification (AEP.L plantation mapped to Consumer Defensive).
- Healthcare/FCF quality caps when trailing FCF negative or Piotroski ≤ 4 (HIK.L sample).

**Prompt — qualitative risk and extraction requirements (38 backlog, 10 recent)**

- Workers not required to flag notice-only files or extract guidance revisions, segment mix, audit-delay language (MEGP.L prompt samples).

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This run is broadly neutral-to-cautious (143 holds vs 17 strong buys and 43 avoids), with buy-tier conviction concentrated in 61 names but top-ranked signals still fresh (46–53% conviction, one week at rating). The largest systemic weakness is **FCF-basis inconsistency**: filing-aligned, screen TTM, and company-adjusted figures diverge materially on ITV.L, FGP.L, and HIK.L, and several names were downgraded from strong buy to buy after FCF overlays—yield- and value-dependent model passes may overstate economic cash generation. A second weakness is **ingest depth vs index breadth**: buy-tier filing indexes are fully bodied (`thin_filing_tickers` empty; `indexed_without_body: 0` across filing_coverage), but initial-mode memo snapshots show low `filings_with_body` ratios (e.g. MEGP.L 16/61, GFTU.L 13/75, GSK.L 20/99), limiting first-pass memo quality to “adequate” (source_quality_score ~0.59–0.69). Gap-fill improved ITV.L, FGP.L, and HIK.L to “strong” memos (0.86–0.96), yet all follow-up questions remain **partially_resolved**—FCF reconciliation, covenant headroom, and US pricing erosion are documented but not closed. These gaps **block full conviction** on top picks: deep analysis assigns watchlist verdicts to all five leaders pending manual FCF and balance-sheet reconciliation.

---

PERSISTENT WEAKNESSES
**Ingest — filing body fetch and classification (dominant backlog theme; 129/287 backlog items, 29/73 recent)**
- Re-pull full RNS/Investegate HTML or PDF bodies instead of Google News wrappers or AI-summary wrappers; recurring for AEP.L (31 indexed, 0 bodies in sample), MEGP.L (52 indexed, 0 bodies), ITV.L, HIK.L, FGP.L.
- Companies House filed-accounts PDF fetch/OCR when bodies missing (AEP.L, ITV.L — five CH refetches returned zero bodies in sample).
- IR presentation PDF extraction for FCF bridges, segment margins, dividend policy (HIK.L, MEGP.L, ITV.L, FGP.L).
- Document dedup and period validation: reject misattributed bodies (HIK.L `ir_a9733d0de6aec27d` identical hash to H1 interim while indexed as April trading update); separate notice-of-results from actual results (MEGP.L).
- Populate missing Yahoo-derived fields (`operating_cashflow` None despite data in `financials_annual.json` — MEGP.L sample).

**Scoring — FCF basis, overlays, and metadata alignment (69 backlog, 16 recent)**
- FCF overlay fires without selecting company-adjusted FCF from RNS reconciliation (FGP.L: filing £362.6M vs company £73.8M; HIK.L: filing $119M vs screen TTM $14.4M).
- Dividend-coverage period mismatches (MEGP.L gross coverage −0.90× from H1 OCF vs FY capex; annual-consistent ~1.68×).
- Yahoo gross D/E and current ratio misstate lease-adjusted leverage (FGP.L D/E 161% vs adjusted net debt £137.7m).
- Sector misclassification (AEP.L plantation mapped to Consumer Defensive).
- Healthcare/FCF quality caps when trailing FCF negative or Piotroski ≤ 4 (HIK.L sample).

**Prompt — qualitative risk and extraction requirements (38 backlog, 10 recent)**
- Governance, pension, covenant, and sector-cycle risks not systematically extracted from assigned bodies (FGP.L pension/covenant; ITV.L governance/FCF question).
- Workers not required to flag notice-only files or extract guidance revisions, segment mix, audit-delay language (MEGP.L prompt samples).

**Coverage / research / ops (smaller clusters)**
- Structured extraction of principal risks, patent cliffs, borrowings covenants (HIK.L coverage; FGP.L ingest).
- Orchestration: select latest dated results bodies, reserve trading-update slots (MEGP.L).
- Attach screen run manifest to gap-fill packs for verifiable universe counts (MEGP.L).

---

THIS WEEK'S FINDINGS
**Gap-fill outcomes**
- `gap_fill.updated: 3`, `created: 0`, `errors: []`, `follow_ups: 3` for ITV.L, FGP.L, HIK.L.

- HIK.L: five questions partially resolved—US Injectables margin guide 27–28% vs 31.0% FY2025, pipeline counts (118 products, 43 launches), net FCF/dividend 0.64× confirmed; patent ledger and external pricing indices still open.
- ITV.L: targeted for gap-fill (FCF triangulation £148M / £212M / £325M, governance) but **no entries in `unresolved_questions`**—ITV follow-ups not closed this pass.

**New / persistent gaps**
- HIK.L IR PDF misattribution: refetched body hash-matches H1 interim, not April trading update.
- FGP.L: 57 body extracts still omit quantified RCF covenant headroom.
- Initial buy-tier memos (MEGP.L, GFTU.L, JSG.L, MGNS.L, AEP.L, IMB.L, GSK.L, KLR.L) remain `adequate` with low body penetration despite high `filings_total` in filing_coverage.

**Verdict shifts**
- Deep analysis: ITV.L, FGP.L, HIK.L signals adjusted strong buy → buy via FCF-basis and sector overlays; all five top picks rated watchlist pending FCF reconciliation.

**Fetch failures / partial success**
- ITV.L: 40 attempted, 30 fetched; bodies 33 → 63 (Investegate 20/30, residual 10/10).
- FGP.L: 41 attempted, 30 fetched; bodies 27 → 57; attempt 2 (CH accounts, IR presentation) fetched 0.

1. **[ingest] Enforce filing-body quality gate: full RNS/PDF fetch, period/headline validation, and content-hash dedup before indexing — expected impact: prevents misattributed bodies (HIK.L), unlocks FCF bridges and risk notes across all gap-fill targets and the ~52-indexed/zero-body MEGP.L-class tickers in backlog.**

rules: Universe: only strong_buy / buy names from the latest screen.
Timing filter: names with timing_signal=wait are excluded from new buys.
Sector cap: at most 1 name(s) per known sector (cap=20%).
Ranking: highest conviction_score first, keep at most 3 names.
Sizing: equal-weight sleeves of current NAV after exits; buys limited by remaining cash.
Hold buffer: full exit only after 2 consecutive rebalance(s) outside the target set.
Re-entry cooldown: wait 1 rebalance(s) after a full exit before buying the same name again.
Dust guard: skip trim/top-up adjustments below £10.
plan.summary: Next rebalance would target 3 equal-weight sleeve(s); leave 2 near-target holding(s).

question_outcomes.question: Is US generic pricing erosion a temporary margin squeeze or a structural reset that makes a 3.9% yield and 12.5× P/E unsafe?

Offsetting: Hikma Rx H1 core margin **20.6%** (+3.0pp); group reiterates **$720–770m** core OP guide (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`); screen P/E **12.5**, yield **3.9%**, growth **~1.7%**. Yield stretched on filing FCF (0.64× net coverage) but not immediately unsafe while OCF exceeds dividends and buyback nears completion.
question_outcomes.next_sources: Post-buyback capital-allocation statement; US generic pricing index time series — external, not ingested
